note: Rule-based scenario simulator. NPC lines and replies are fixed, reviewed basic Hindi consistent with the existing phrase bank and lessons. This is NOT AI and is never described as AI.

scenarios.title: Meeting someone
scenarios.context: You are introduced to someone for the first time. They greet you in Hindi.

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that answers the greeting.

choices.text: मैं ठीक हूँ, धन्यवाद। आप कैसे हैं?
choices.roman: main theek hoon, dhanyavaad. aap kaise hain?
choices.en: I am fine, thank you. How are you?

choices.note: A valid sentence, but it does not answer the greeting.

steps.explanation: The polite reply is मैं ठीक हूँ (main theek hoon) — "I am fine" — and you return the question with आप कैसे हैं?

steps.npc: मैं भी ठीक हूँ। आपका नाम क्या है?
steps.npc_roman: main bhi theek hoon. aapka naam kya hai?
steps.npc_en: I am fine too. What is your name?
steps.prompt: Choose the reply that gives your name.

choices.note: This does not tell them your name.

steps.explanation: मेरा नाम … है (mera naam … hai) is the pattern for "My name is …". Fill in your own name.

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that says "nice to meet you too".

choices.note: True, maybe — but not a reply to the introduction.

steps.explanation: Add भी (bhi, "too") to return the compliment: आपसे मिलकर भी खुशी हुई।

scenarios.completion: You handled a first meeting: greet, exchange names, and part politely. That is the single most-used pattern in spoken Hindi.

scenarios.title: Ordering food
scenarios.context: You sit down in a small restaurant in India. The server comes to your table.

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that orders food.
steps.explanation: Order with the item + कृपया (kripya, "please"): एक रोटी और दाल, कृपया।

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that politely declines.

choices.note: You could ask this, but not in answer to "anything else".

steps.explanation: बस इतना ही (bas itna hi) means "just this much" — the standard polite stop.

choices.note: Not a reply to being served.

steps.explanation: धन्यवाद (dhanyavaad) is the safe thank-you; in casual speech शुक्रिया (shukriya) is just as common.

scenarios.completion: You ordered, stopped the order politely, and thanked the server. Enough to eat in Hindi anywhere.

scenarios.title: Taking a taxi
scenarios.context: You get into an auto-rickshaw or taxi. The driver turns to you.

steps.npc_en: Where do you want to go?
steps.prompt: Choose the reply that gives a destination.
steps.explanation: Destination + कृपया (kripya) is all you need: होटल ताज, कृपया।

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that asks the fare.

choices.note: Ask the fare before you agree — not about food.

steps.explanation: कितना (kitna, "how much") + पैसा (paisa, "money"): कितना पैसा लगेगा? Agree the fare up front.

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that pays and thanks.
steps.explanation: यह रहा (yeh raha, "here it is") hands over the money; add धन्यवाद (dhanyavaad).

scenarios.completion: You gave a destination, agreed a fare, and paid. The whole ride in three lines.

scenarios.title: At a shop
scenarios.context: You are in a market stall looking at goods. The shopkeeper notices you.

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that points at something.

choices.note: You were asked what you want, not how you are.

steps.explanation: मुझे … चाहिए (mujhe … chahiye) is "I want/need …" — point and say मुझे यह चाहिए।

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that asks for a lower price.

choices.note: That ends an order; it does not bargain.

steps.explanation: थोड़ा कम (thoda kam, "a little less") + कीजिए (kijiye, polite "do"): थोड़ा कम कीजिए? Bargaining is normal in markets.

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that agrees and pays.

choices.note: That is a taxi-driver's question, not a shop answer.

steps.explanation: यह लीजिए (yeh lijiye) is the polite "here you are" when handing something over.

scenarios.completion: You asked for something, bargained once, and paid. Market shopping without a word of English.

scenarios.title: Meeting family
scenarios.context: You visit relatives after a long time. An elder greets you at the door.

steps.npc_en: Namaste, we met after many days.
steps.prompt: Choose the reply that greets back respectfully.

choices.note: Thirsty or not, greet the elder first.

steps.explanation: With elders, always the respectful आप (aap). नमस्ते, आप कैसे हैं? is the safe opening.

steps.npc: मैं ठीक हूँ। घर पर सब कैसे हैं?
steps.npc_roman: main theek hoon. ghar par sab kaise hain?
steps.npc_en: I am fine. How is everyone at home?
steps.prompt: Choose the reply that says everyone is well.

choices.note: Not the answer to how the family is.

steps.explanation: सब (sab, "all/everyone") + ठीक हैं (theek hain, "are fine"): सब ठीक हैं।

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that says you have eaten.

choices.note: That answers neither the meal nor the moment.

steps.explanation: खा लिया (kha liya) is the completion form of "to eat": हाँ, खा लिया। In Indian homes this question is hospitality, not just a question.

scenarios.completion: You greeted an elder respectfully, asked after the family, and answered the classic Indian hospitality question.

scenarios.title: Asking for help
scenarios.context: Something is wrong and you need help. A person stops next to you.

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that asks for help.

choices.note: If you are fine, you do not need to stop people.

steps.explanation: मदद (madad, "help") + चाहिए (chahiye): मुझे मदद चाहिए। The single most important sentence to know.

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that points at the pain.

choices.note: They asked you; don't bounce it back.

steps.prompt: Choose the reply that thanks them.

choices.note: Later. First thank the person helping.

steps.explanation: धन्यवाद (dhanyavaad) — the same thank-you carries every situation.

scenarios.completion: You asked for help, described where it hurt, and thanked the person helping. For anything serious, always call the local emergency number too.
